component.name: ai-tool
component.title: AI Tool
component.description: Expose a Camel route as a tool that a model calls through a Camel AI producer, or that MCP clients call through the Camel MCP server.
component.label: ai

argSchema.label: consumer
argSchema.description: The JSON Schema of the tool input, inline or loaded from a resource such as classpath:schema.json or file:schema.json, for input that the parameter options cannot describe, such as nested objects, arrays and oneOf. The root must be an object schema with at least one property, and the route receives each top-level argument as a header. When the schema does not set additionalProperties, Camel adds additionalProperties: false, so a client that validates the input (such as the MCP server) refuses an undeclared argument. Cannot be combined with the parameter options.

argumentsAsBody.label: consumer
argumentsAsBody.description: Whether the route also receives the arguments of the call as a JSON object in the message body, as a String. The body holds the same arguments as the headers, so undeclared arguments and names that start with camel are left out. When false, the route starts without a body.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

configuration.description: The configuration that every endpoint starts from. The endpoint copies it, and the options of the endpoint URI replace its values.

description.label: consumer
description.description: The description of what the tool does, which the model reads as is to decide when to call the tool, and which MCP clients see in tools/list. If not set or blank, the tool name is used.

destructiveHint.label: consumer
destructiveHint.description: MCP hint that the tool may perform destructive or irreversible updates. Advisory for MCP clients; not enforced by Camel.

idempotentHint.label: consumer
idempotentHint.description: MCP hint that repeating the tool call with the same arguments has no additional effect. Advisory for MCP clients; not enforced by Camel.

openWorldHint.label: consumer
openWorldHint.description: MCP hint that the tool interacts with external systems outside the application's control. Advisory for MCP clients; not enforced by Camel.

outputParameters.label: consumer
outputParameters.description: The fields of the structured output of the tool, set as outputParameter.NAME=TYPE and outputParameter.NAME.description=TEXT, from which Camel builds the output JSON Schema that MCP clients see in tools/list. TYPE is string, integer, number or boolean. When set, the route must reply with a JSON body, which the MCP server returns as structured content. Cannot be combined with outputSchema. This is a multi-value option with prefix: outputParameter.

outputSchema.label: consumer
outputSchema.description: The JSON Schema of the structured output of the tool, inline or loaded from a resource such as classpath:result.json, which MCP clients see in tools/list. When set, the route must reply with a JSON body, which the MCP server returns as structured content. Cannot be combined with the outputParameter options.

parameters.label: consumer
parameters.description: The input parameters of the tool, set as parameter.NAME=TYPE, parameter.NAME.description=TEXT, parameter.NAME.required=true or false and parameter.NAME.enum=VALUE1,VALUE2, from which Camel builds the JSON Schema of the tool input. TYPE is string, integer, number or boolean, and string when not set or not known. The route receives each argument as a header named NAME, and a call without a required argument is refused before the route runs. Cannot be combined with argSchema. This is a multi-value option with prefix: parameter.

readOnlyHint.label: consumer
readOnlyHint.description: MCP hint that the tool only reads data and does not modify state. Advisory for MCP clients; not enforced by Camel.

returnDirect.label: consumer
returnDirect.description: Whether the openai producer ends its tool loop with the result of this tool as the reply, without sending the result back to the model. It does so only when every tool that the model called in that turn sets returnDirect. The other AI producers ignore it, and some MCP server engines publish it to clients as a tool annotation.

searchable.label: consumer
searchable.description: When true, this route tool is eligible for tool search and is omitted from the initial model request while the producer has tool search enabled. When false, the tool stays directly visible to the model. Searchability is a visibility policy, not an authorization policy, and has no effect when tool search is disabled.

tags.label: consumer
tags.description: A comma-separated list of tags to register the tool under. An AI producer (such as openai, langchain4j-agent or spring-ai-chat) offers the model the tools of the tags in its own tags option, and the MCP server exposes the tools whose tags match its tag patterns. Without tags, the tool goes into a default pool that is added to every tag a producer selects, and that the MCP server never exposes.

title.label: consumer
title.description: The human-readable title of the tool, which MCP clients can show in tools/list instead of the name. The AI producers do not send it to the model. If not set, the tool has no title.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

allowedRoles.label: consumer,security
allowedRoles.description: Comma-separated list of the roles a caller needs to call the tool, for example finance,controlling. Any one of them is enough unless allRolesRequired is set. The roles are checked before the route runs, against the caller's roles in the exchange property CamelAiToolSecurityPrincipalRoles: a call without that property is refused. A value that is set but names no role refuses every call. Set it on the component as the default of every tool route, or per endpoint to replace it.

allRolesRequired.label: consumer,security
allRolesRequired.description: Whether the caller needs all the roles in allowedRoles, rather than any one of them. Has no effect when allowedRoles is not set.

authorizationPolicy.label: consumer,security
authorizationPolicy.description: Reference to an org.apache.camel.spi.AuthorizationPolicy used to authorize tool calls before the route runs. Set it on the component to guard every tool route by construction, or per endpoint to override. The policy authorizes on trustworthy input only: the tool name comes from the route (never from model output), and the caller identity is carried as an exchange property set before the agent ran (for example by camel-spiffe or camel-keycloak), which the model cannot set. Authorize on exchange properties or validated tokens only, never on message headers (on a tool route the headers carry the model-controlled tool arguments). A denied call surfaces to the model as a short refusal rather than a stack trace.

CamelAiToolCallId.label: consumer
CamelAiToolCallId.description: The tool invocation identifier supplied by the calling framework. Set when an in-process producer (such as openai or langchain4j-agent) calls the tool. Absent when the framework does not supply one, such as for a call over MCP, where the bridge has no tool call id.

CamelAiToolConversationId.label: consumer
CamelAiToolConversationId.description: The conversation identifier supplied by the calling framework. Absent when the framework does not supply one.

consumerOut.description: No body: each argument of the tool call is a header named as its parameter, a Map or a List for a nested JSON value. Undeclared arguments and names starting with camel are dropped

consumerReply.description: The tool result, as text: the body converted to a String, so a Map, a List or a POJO is sent as its toString(): marshal it to JSON first. No body gives No result. With outputSchema or outputParameter.NAME options the body must be JSON: a JSON String, a Map, a List, a number or a boolean, and bytes, a stream or another object fail the call

toolName.description: The name of the tool, which the model sees and uses to call it, and which MCP clients see in tools/list. It must not contain a slash. A route whose tool name is already registered under one of its tags, or in the pool of tools without tags, fails to start.

exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.
